## ⚠️ The order's first instruction targets the one claim this card did NOT measure itself

The card marks it honestly — **[CARD-CLAIM, measured by the objectui#9941 dev against the BUILT schema, ⛔ not re-run by this seat]** — that the node copied verbatim is refused with `invalid_type` at path `["items"]`. The dev was told to re-run exactly that before writing a single corrected key, and to take the whole four-row key table first-hand against `packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts`, including whether `content` really carries no `.optional()`.

⭐ The card's own control is carried into the order: `defaultValue` is a key the `tabs` renderer really does read, so an instrument that finds `defaultValue` and not `lazyLoad` has distinguished 「member of this node」 from 「string present in the repo」. An instrument that finds neither is broken, ⛔ not a finding.

## The card's open question is the order's SECOND instruction, and it is a stop condition, not a footnote

This card deliberately took no measurement of whether the platform lazy-loads tab bodies at all, and said so:

> ⭐ Whoever takes it must settle that first: a corrected example that still promises an optimization nothing performs is the same defect with better spelling.

The dev was told to measure it — what `lazyLoad` on `usePerformance` actually gates, and whether any `tabs` rendering path reaches it — and then to take ONE of two routes, **justified from the measurement rather than from taste**: fix the keys AND correct the prose to name the real trigger and where that knob lives (a hook configuration object, ⛔ not a node member); or, if nothing keeps the promise, remove the promise. ⛔ Splitting the difference — fixing the keys and leaving the sentence — is named in the order as the outcome the card already rejected.

The PR body is required to state which route was taken and the measurement that decided it.

## Also in the order

The ```` ```json ```` fence contains a JavaScript comment, so a copied example fails to parse before it ever reaches the schema. Whatever survives must be valid JSON under that tag — and if a doc-fence gate would have caught it, the dev is to report why it did not, ⛔ not widen this PR to fix the gate.

`check:doc-snippets` answering `PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2)` is pre-declared in the order as ⛔ NOT a pass — it must be recorded as not-a-verdict.

## ⛔ Fenced out

objectui#9941 (the shipped `defaultProps` seed in `packages/components`) is named as do-not-touch. Reads outside `content/docs/**` are encouraged; edits outside it are a STOP.

## Landing is this seat's

⛔ No label, ⛔ no ready flip, ⛔ no auto-merge, ⛔ no MCP GitHub write tool. The PR stays DRAFT.
